arguments.query: Indoors, under a large rocket stage hanging from the ceiling, people in white spacesuit costumes stand among huge white letters while a crowd watches behind them.
An outdoor crowd cheers with arms raised in the air, and a woman in large black sunglasses smiles in the front.
A tall orange and white rocket stands between lightning towers on the launch pad, with a white water tower on the left and a blue sky behind.
An astronaut in an orange suit, wearing a closed helmet with the visor up, sits in a red chair while someone says shivers have run up and down his spine many times.

After an astronaut in an orange suit and helmet leans back in his chair and makes hand signs with gloved hands, a crew member in an orange suit salutes from a red chair, and then two suited astronauts sit talking while a blonde technician helps them.
In a wide view of a white suit-up room, a man in an orange suit sits on the left while technicians in white bend over another crew member reclined in a red chair.
A fisheye camera on the launch tower looks down the side of the rocket as the engines at its base ignite in a burst of bright light, with the number 813 visible near the top of the frame.

While a voice says the question isn't go or not go but whether you will lead or follow, a smiling woman in an orange suit with an American flag patch sits by a control panel and looks toward a technician.
After a shot of an empty doorway under a purple banner with crew names on it, four astronauts in orange suits stand in a row in front of that doorway.
A woman in a light green blazer stands at a microphone in front of tall windows and throws both arms out wide in celebration.
An onboard camera looks back at a spacecraft section with a gleaming engine nozzle against black space, with bright light flaring along its lower edge.
A woman in a green blazer speaks into a handheld microphone in front of large windows and says their greatest chapters are yet to be written.

After a woman at a microphone throws her arms wide in celebration, an onboard camera shows a long side booster with fire at its base pulling away from the rocket, then a different view shows curved panels drifting away from a white surface against a dark sky.
A blue title card that says "NEXT" next to an animated Earth with a small Moon and a curved orbit path, with a caption saying the crew's nearly 10-day mission will take them around the Moon and back.

While a speaker says the Moon has now become the center and focus of the mission, an animated spacecraft with solar panel arms flies high above Earth's curved edge, and then the view cuts to a close-up of cratered lunar surface.

After a large outdoor crowd cheers and films with phones, two rocket boosters drift apart in the sky, trailing smoke. Then a person seen in silhouette behind tall angled windows watches the exhaust plume climb.
The curved, cratered edge of the Moon fills the lower part of the frame, and a small blue-and-white Earth peeks over the lunar horizon against black space.
A close-up of a woman with glasses studying a computer screen at a console, with an older man in a suit working beside her in a control room.
While a voice repeats "oh, oh, oh" over and over, the dark disc of the Moon sits in front of a glowing white halo of light in space.
A close-up of a man with glasses studying a computer screen at a console, with an older man in a suit working beside him in a control room.
Seen from above, three red-and-white striped parachutes lower a capsule onto a deep blue ocean, and white spray rises where it touches the water.
A helicopter with its rotors turning sits on the grey flight deck of a ship out at sea, filmed from a high angle with the ocean all around.
Two smiling astronauts in orange flight suits sit side by side inside a helicopter, and the screen then cuts to the blue NASA logo on a black background.
After a capsule hanging from three striped parachutes splashes down in dark blue water, a high shot shows a helicopter on the deck of a ship at sea.
Seen from above, two red-and-white striped parachutes lower a capsule onto a deep blue ocean, and white spray rises where it touches the water.
Four astronauts in orange pressure suits stand side by side on a striped walkway, posing in front of a building with NASA logos on its wall.
While a voice says they are going for their teammates, an astronaut in an orange suit and an open-visor helmet makes a heart shape with gloved hands toward the camera.
After four astronauts in orange suits pose in a row on a walkway, they walk past a crowd of people who cheer and hold up phones to take pictures.
As the announcer says 'liftoff' and that the crew is now bound for the moon, the rocket climbs off the pad above a huge grey cloud of exhaust.

After the rocket rises off the pad above a billowing smoke cloud, a crowd of spectators, one in a NASA sweatshirt, hold up phones to film it, and then the rocket climbs through a blue sky trailing a long bright flame.
The full, grey, cratered Moon fills the middle of a plain black frame, with nothing else in view.
Inside a cluttered spacecraft cabin with an American flag hanging overhead, four crew members in dark jackets float close together. One of them speaks into a handheld microphone.

An astronaut's dark silhouette looks out a window at the bright blue-and-white Earth. Then the view changes to a close-up of a man's ear and cheek, with the small Moon far off in the black window behind him.
As a voice announces that Houston is go for TLI, the camera shows a mission control room full of people seated at desks with monitors.

First the small Moon shows through a square spacecraft window framed by cables and padding. Next the full grey Moon appears alone on black. Last the Moon hangs beside the curved white edge of the spacecraft.
A dark crescent of the Moon fills the lower frame against black space, with a small crescent Earth peeking over the upper-left edge of the lunar limb.
A completely dark Moon sits in the center of the frame, surrounded by a soft white glowing halo of sunlight against black space during an eclipse.
Four astronauts in dark matching shirts pose together inside a cramped spacecraft cabin beneath American and Canadian flags, with a small plush toy floating in front of them.
While a voice lists "coffee, moon, joy," astronauts float smiling and laughing inside a cluttered capsule under Canadian and American flags.
After a shot of the eclipsed Moon as a black disk ringed by bright white light, four astronauts crowd into a selfie wearing colorful paper eclipse glasses.
Three astronauts squeeze together for a close-up selfie inside the spacecraft, all wearing colorful paper eclipse glasses.
A spacecraft's solar array panel sits in the foreground on the left while a half-lit Earth hangs in black space, and the pink caption "SAFE RETURN" appears.
A capsule floats in the ocean, ringed by an orange inflatable collar and topped with red-orange balloons, while recovery crews sit in a raft beside it.

After a large white piece of spacecraft hardware is moved along a road on a transporter with a "LET'S GO!" banner, the rocket is shown standing on its launch tower with an American flag, and then a crowd of spectators cheers with their arms raised.
Three green-and-white striped parachutes lower a capsule toward a dark blue ocean while pink text about the crew being the first humans to fly around the Moon in over 50 years is shown.
While the speaker thanks the international partners who make the mission possible, workers stand around the base of a huge white spacecraft section marked with NASA and ESA logos.
On a black screen, the Artemis logo appears and then gives way to the blue ESA logo.
A full moon hangs against a black background, then a night image of the lit rocket on its launch tower fades in over the moon's surface.
A crowd of spectators cheers at night under a 'Space Center' sign. In front, a masked man wears a grey NASA sweatshirt and people wave small American flags.
A wide shot of a launch control room with tall slanted windows and rows of desks covered in computer monitors, with staff seated at the consoles.
In the launch control room, a woman with long reddish hair stands and speaks into a headset, giving the go to resume the count and launch Artemis-1. A man in a suit stands behind her.
A crowd of spectators cheers at night under a 'Space Center' sign. In front, a masked man wears a red NASA sweatshirt and people wave small American flags.
A cheering crowd at night waves small American flags. A man in front wears a green NASA sweatshirt, and the on-screen caption reads Space Center Houston.
A wide view of a launch control room with rows of wooden consoles and computer monitors, where many staff sit and stand watching.
A woman in glasses speaks into a handheld microphone in front of tall angled windows and says they showed the space coast tonight and what a beautiful view it is.
An older man in a dark suit jacket and light blue open-collar shirt speaks at a microphone in front of a large American flag backdrop.
The round blue NASA logo with its red swoosh appears on a plain black background.
A black cone-shaped space capsule with large yellow flotation balloons on top bobs in choppy blue ocean water, with a small motorboat carrying crew right behind it.
Seen from above, a group of sailors in dark uniforms crowd around black inflatable boats on a wet, sloped ship deck that leads down to the sea.
The open stern well deck of a large gray navy ship faces the camera, with a capsule topped by yellow balloons floating in the water in front of it beside a small boat.
A woman in a black jacket stands in front of a black capsule topped with yellow balloons inside a ship's hangar and gestures toward it as she says that behind her is the crew module test article.

After a gray navy ship is seen far off on the horizon past the curved edge of a hull, the ship's open stern is shown with a floating capsule and a small boat. Then a woman in black stands in front of the capsule on a ship's deck.
Dark title card with the words "HOW TO TRAIN THE RECOVERY TEAM" over silhouettes of people running, then the video cuts to a presenter in front of a pool.
A man in a dark polo shirt stands in front of a large indoor training pool with a capsule mockup and says he is the EGS open water lead for the Orion and Artemis missions.

After an underwater shot looking down at a submerged spacecraft mockup, a wide view shows the huge indoor pool with flags along the walls. Next, a capsule mockup floats beside a yellow inflatable raft in the pool.
In a huge indoor training pool, a capsule sits on a yellow inflatable raft with a group of divers crowded on it. A row of national flags hangs on the wall behind them.
Poolside, a group of young men in navy-blue T-shirts stand around listening. One of them, in a camouflage cap, has "DEEP SEA" printed in yellow on the back of his shirt.
Over a dark, grey shot of a navy ship at sea, a white on-screen caption reads "PERFORMING THE UNDERWAY RECOVERY TEST".

After crew members in tan uniforms and harnesses work around an orange cylinder on a raft, a caption about performing the underway recovery test appears over a ship at sea. Then a capsule floats in open ocean waves while a small boat approaches.
Poolside, a group of young men in navy-blue T-shirts stand around listening. One of them, in a camouflage cap, has "NAVY DIVER" printed in yellow on the back of his shirt.
A gray Navy helicopter hovers low over a ship's flight deck under a clear blue sky.

A woman in a black jacket stands in front of a capsule with yellow balloons and says the first day of nearly every recovery starts with what they call 'in and outs', to train the ship on handling the test article.
After a gray amphibious ship is seen at sea with its stern well deck open, a capsule with yellow balloons floats right in front of the open stern gate.
A rescuer in a red and black suit is lowered on a cable from a helicopter against a bright blue sky.
A gray Navy helicopter hovers low over the open ocean, seen head-on against a pale sky.
After a close-up of an American flag patch on the shoulder of an orange suit, a round mission patch on an orange sleeve is shown, then a gloved hand adjusts the wrist of an orange suit.
Seen from below, a person dangles from a hoist cable against a grey sky, and then a helicopter hovers low over the choppy sea.
On a ship's flight deck, crew members in helmets walk a person in an orange suit away from a grey helicopter whose rotors are still turning.
A sailor in camouflage uniform and a moustache sits in a hangar next to grey inflatable boats and explains that the front porch is an inflatable life raft that attaches to the capsule.
After two inflatable boats full of divers speed across rough blue water, a wide shot shows a capsule with yellow balloons floating near a raft, with a large navy ship on the horizon.
Seen from above, a large crowd poses together on a ship's flight deck, holding up an American flag, with several people in bright green shirts at the left edge.
A bearded man in a black cap and glasses, wearing a navy polo shirt, looks down at something in a dim control area.
After a man in a red life vest and a woman write at a desk, an older bearded man points at something while workers in brown hard hats look on.
Seen from space, a capsule with its nose cone open approaches against the black sky, with Earth's curved horizon below.
A white-domed space capsule rides on an orange multi-wheeled KAMAG transporter along a road under a purple dusk sky, headlights on.
A tall orange rocket core stage stands upright inside a dark assembly building, lit from below, with tall steel work platforms on either side.
While the narrator says an astronaut has been named commander of the next crewed Starliner mission, an astronaut in a blue flight suit poses with his arms crossed against a black background.
A white-domed space capsule rides on an orange multi-wheeled KAMAG transporter along a road under a bright blue midday sky.
A tall rocket with an orange core stage and two white side boosters lifts off beside its launch tower, with flames and thick white smoke at its base.
Seen through a cockpit head-up display, green flight symbols and heading numbers are laid over the long pointed nose of a jet flying above desert terrain.
A man in a dark suit with a red striped tie speaks to the camera against a dark background, and then the round blue NASA logo with a red swoosh appears on black.
While the narrator says the aircraft reached Mach 1.53, just over a thousand miles an hour, a white long-nosed supersonic jet flies against a deep blue sky with a chase jet nearby.

After a white NASA jet with a very long pointed nose rolls down a desert runway and is then seen in flight high above a dry lakebed, the view switches to a cockpit head-up display looking out over the same long nose.
A man in a cap and grey short-sleeve shirt sits smiling and holds a large camera, while another man in a backwards cap leans in to photograph him in a training facility.
A rendered space telescope with a flat white sunshade drifts through black space, then the view becomes a deep field full of many small galaxies.
As the narrator says NASA is making major progress towards Artemis 3, a wide shot shows a rocket core stage's engine section held in tall blue scaffolding inside a large assembly hall.

A close-up shows a Falcon Heavy lifting off from the pad in a burst of flame, with a T+ 00:00:03 launch clock on screen. After that, a wide view shows the rocket climbing above billowing clouds of exhaust.
In a hangar, a man in glasses and a short-sleeve button shirt stands at a workbench next to a man in a green Hawaiian floral shirt, and they handle equipment on the table.
Three men in dark caps sit side by side inside a white spacecraft cabin mockup. The two on the left hold large professional cameras while the man on the right smiles.
A close-up, helmet-camera-style view of a white spacesuit's arm and torso, with loose white tether straps and a silver cylindrical fitting, against dark station hardware.
A spacewalker in a white suit works on the exterior of the space station among its large white modules, with the curve of Earth's horizon and black space in the background.
While the narrator says it's been a busy stretch of spacewalks aboard the International Space Station, the camera looks down past a robotic arm and station hardware to white clouds over Earth.
Three men in dark caps sit side by side inside a white spacecraft cabin mockup. The two on the left hold clipboards while the man on the right smiles.

After a close view of a rocket rising on a bright flame above billowing exhaust clouds at the launch pad, a wide shot from across the water shows the rocket climbing into a hazy sky, and then the blue NASA logo appears on a black screen.

A grey, cratered lunar surface seen from directly overhead flips back and forth between before-and-after images: a small fresh crater with bright ejecta rays spreading out to one side appears in the middle, then disappears to leave an older crater with no rays, then appears again.
A drone shot over a wooded research campus, with a large hangar marked Langley Research Center in the foreground and a white dome in the distance.
As the narrator says researchers used pressure-sensitive paint at Langley Research Center, two men in front of wall monitors sit at a control console, one wearing a headset.

A blonde woman in a black polka-dot sleeveless dress stands talking in front of an American flag and a flag with the NASA seal, then the screen cuts to the NASA meatball logo alone on a black background.
A woman in a polka-dot dress in front of the US flag and the NASA seal says each test, flight and mission brings us closer to turning the near impossible into reality, then signs off until next time.
A split-screen view looks up at a descent stage covered in silver foil while, below it, a rover hangs from cables over a dusty brown surface.
An animated orange-red planet floats against a black, star-speckled background.

A man in a gray plaid suit and dark tie stands with his hands clasped between an American flag and a dark blue flag with a round emblem. The screen then cuts to a blue round logo with a red swoosh on black.

As the narrator says that from the historic touchdown to today's ongoing discoveries the mission continues to shape our path, a rover's white body and wheel sit in the foreground of a flat, rocky reddish plain.
Close-up of a hand holding a vacuum-sealed plastic pouch of green, herb-flecked food with two round blue dots stuck on it.
Wearing a grey polo shirt and khaki trousers, an astronaut holds a handheld microphone and floats inside a white space station module with a round hatch behind him and stowage bags on the walls.
While the narrator says NASA astronaut Chris Williams joined in the excitement about Artemis II, an astronaut in a grey polo floats in a space station module and speaks into a handheld microphone.
Satellite-style overhead photo of a launch pad on the coast, with a red arrow pointing at the rocket and its shadow, then a wider view of the Florida coastline and a runway from orbit.
A man in a navy suit with his hands clasped speaks in front of an American flag and the NASA seal, and then the shot cuts to the NASA logo on a black background.
While the narrator says the astronaut photographed the rocket and its shadow from nearly 250 miles above Kennedy Space Center, a red arrow marks the rocket on an orbital photo of the launch pad.
A host in a suit and tie standing in front of an American flag and the NASA seal says thanks for watching and that they'll see you next time on the NASA Minute.
After a wide orbital view of the coast captioned 'Kennedy Space Center from nearly 250 miles above', a suited host in front of flags signs off and the NASA logo appears.
Overhead orbital photo of a launch pad on the coast, with a yellow circle drawn around the rocket and its shadow.
Grayscale spacecraft view of a planet's surface, with a bright, ragged white ice cap in the upper left against a darker cratered terrain.

While the narrator says NASA officially welcomed Matt Anderson, a man raises his right hand in front of a row of American flags as a woman holding a book stands between him and another man in a dark suit.
Studio portrait of a smiling man with short hair in a dark suit and a solid green tie, posed in front of an American flag and a NASA seal on a blue background.
The space station, with its long solar arrays spread out, floats against a bright blue and white Earth that curves away at the edge of the frame.
A large red sculpture of the curvy NASA 'worm' logo stands on a paved plaza in front of a grey office building.
Inside a cluttered space station module, a man in a grey t-shirt and a woman with her hair in a bun lean in close as they work on equipment at a wall of hardware.

While the narrator tells viewers to tune in to hear about progress on humanity's first lunar outpost, an animation shows astronauts working on the grey lunar surface near a large pressurized rover and a small American flag.
A large blue sculpture of the curvy NASA 'worm' logo stands on a paved plaza in front of a grey office building.

After a crowd looks up and points phones at the sky, people standing on a shoreline watch the rocket climb far away across the water, and then the rocket climbs into a deep blue sky trailing a white plume.
After side-by-side close-up portraits of two astronauts in orange suits, the four crew members in orange suits pose together for a group portrait.
A large crowd stands behind a wooden picket fence near the water, raising phones as a rocket climbs into the sky in the distance.

On a ship's deck, an astronaut in an orange suit points one finger up as he walks between two military rescuers. Next, a grinning astronaut in an orange suit raises his fist behind a crew member in a dark vest. After that, a female astronaut in an orange suit and a navy cap waves her arm high near a helmeted rescuer.

A female astronaut in an orange suit raises her arm in celebration on a ship's deck. Next, two astronauts in orange suits sit side by side in a helicopter's open doorway while a soldier in camouflage and purple gloves stands beside them.
Looking past the edge of a solar array, a thin bright crescent of Earth hangs in black space, with a purple lens flare above it.

After a close-up of red NASA lettering on the side of the shiny spacecraft, the view widens to show the capsule's blue reflective surface with the NASA logo and an American flag. Then a small crescent glows in a nearly black frame.
A close view of the moon's grey surface packed with craters, with one large crater on the left that has a central peak.
Four red-and-white striped parachutes lower a capsule toward a dark blue ocean, while pink text says the crew are the first humans to fly around the Moon in over 50 years.
While a speaker says "this is a relay race," a group crowded inside a station module talks into a microphone, with US and Canadian flags and an "America 250" sign behind them.
A seated crowd fills an indoor hall at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center, under a huge rocket stage hanging from the ceiling. Large white NASA letters stand in the foreground.

After a fisheye close-up of the rocket clearing the tower in a shower of sparks, a wide night shot shows it rising on a bright flame between the launch towers. Then a lit crowd of spectators waves flags as they watch.
A seated crowd fills an indoor hall at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center, under a huge rocket stage hanging from the ceiling. Large red NASA letters stand in the foreground.
A gray-haired man in a suit at a podium in front of a starry backdrop says the James Webb Space Telescope shows how big and vast the universe is and that there's a lot out there to explore.
Three people in flight helmets and green flight suits walk across a ship's deck, with crew in green shirts standing behind them.

After a wide shot of a capsule mockup floating in an indoor pool next to a yellow inflatable raft, with a row of national flags on the wall behind, people in tan shirts load a person in a helmet into a wire rescue basket that holds an orange float.

A capsule is seen far off through the open stern of a dark, flooded ship well deck. Next, a closer view shows the capsule floating inside the well deck next to a yellow frame, while people watch from a railing above.
After a small boat crew approaches a capsule with red balloons in the open ocean in footage labelled Artemis I Mission, the capsule with red balloons is pulled toward the open well deck of a ship.

While a speaker describes the stability collar as an inflatable ring that goes around it, a seen-from-above shot shows a capsule with yellow balloons on top, ringed by an orange float, with a small gray inflatable boat beside it.
On a ship's flight deck, a crew member in a green jacket raises an arm toward a distant helicopter while two others stand nearby watching.
A woman with long reddish-brown hair, wearing a dark top, speaks in an interview against a dark background with blue and white cables behind her.

Seen from behind, two men look at computer monitors. One wears a dark hoodie with a red hood and a graphic printed on the back, and a small yellow-and-white capsule model is visible in the background.
After a man in a dark suit and tie speaks into a microphone at a press conference table, a white rocket with a capsule on top lifts off at night next to the launch tower in a bright burst of flame.
In a training facility, a man in a light blue short-sleeved shirt handles equipment on a table. Next to him, a man in a green Hawaiian shirt smiles.
A woman with long wavy blonde hair and a black button-front dress speaks to the camera, then waves goodbye. Behind her are an American flag and a dark blue NASA flag.
Through the round open door of a huge vacuum chamber, a tall lander frame wrapped in gold foil stands inside, lit with blue light against rows of vertical panels.

After a white rocket lifts off at night from a launch tower in billowing white smoke, a close-up shows a gloved technician in a hairnet working on a small silver CubeSat box next to an open protective case.
A worker in a white coat stands on the floor beside a giant cream-colored vacuum chamber door with a NASA logo, which is swung open. A red forklift is parked next to it.
Animated diagram on a dark blue background labeled DART: a small moonlet orbits a larger rocky asteroid along an elliptical path, with an Earth icon in the lower left corner.
Low-angle shot of a boxy metal observatory building at night with a starry sky overhead, a red-lit opening in its side and a black spherical dish in front.
While the narrator says the spacecraft struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos in 2022, a lumpy gray boulder-covered asteroid grows larger against a black background.
A man in a dark suit and red tie speaks to the camera while standing in front of a United Nations flag and a NASA seal.

After a shot of a gold-foil cargo spacecraft drifting away from the station's robotic arm above Earth's clouds, a man in a suit stands in front of an American flag and a NASA seal and starts speaking.
Lab monitors show a temperature reading of 3102.1°F next to a red-glowing thermal image, under a wall sign reading 'Development and Test Facility'.

While the narrator says technologies like this could help astronauts live and work sustainably on the moon, an animation shows suited astronauts and a lunar rover near domed habitats on the gray lunar surface.
A title card over a reddish planet edge reads 'Deep Space Food Challenge' with 'Mars to Table' in large letters below it.

A woman with long blonde hair, wearing a light blue belted wrap dress, talks and gestures with both hands. She stands in front of an American flag and a dark blue flag that carries a round agency seal. The shot then cuts to the blue NASA meatball logo on a black background.
A fisheye camera looks down the side of the rocket at its side boosters and core engines as bright flames burst out of the engine nozzles at ignition, lighting up the pad below.
Wide shot across low scrub: the tall orange-and-white rocket rises off its launch pad between thin lightning towers, with a huge white exhaust cloud billowing out to the left along the ground.

A camera mounted on the rocket looks down its silver side as a side booster's nose fires bright orange separation thrusters, and the booster tilts and drifts away from the vehicle, with the ground far below.
Shot from above over deep blue ocean, a capsule hanging under three red-and-white striped parachutes hits the water and throws up a white splash.
Aerial view of a gray ship's flight deck at sea. A helicopter sits on the deck markings with its rotor blades turning.

Seen from a distance, a tall orange rocket with white side boosters lifts off its launch tower, riding a bright flame above huge grey-white exhaust clouds spreading across the pad, with a water tower on the right
Seen from space against a blue Earth, the cone-shaped crew capsule drifts away from the cylindrical service module after separating from it
The small dark capsule falls through a hazy pale sky hanging below a pair of small drogue parachutes on long lines
Night close-up of the base of a huge orange rocket between two white side boosters: its main engines ignite, glowing bright pink-white, and red-lit exhaust clouds billow out beneath the stage.
Fisheye camera on the launch tower at night: the rocket rises past the tower structure on a blinding burst of engine fire, with sparks and debris spraying across the frame
Wide night shot from far away: the rocket lifts off the pad between the lightning towers, and glowing exhaust clouds billow out sideways along the ground
Tracking shot against a black sky: the rocket keeps climbing on a bright flame at its base, and its glowing exhaust plume trails behind it as it goes up
A black cone-shaped capsule topped with yellow inflated balloons rocks in choppy open sea, with water splashing around its base, while a small boat with crew sits just behind it
A black capsule with yellow balloons on top floats inside a flooded ship well deck toward a yellow metal frame, then sits in the yellow cradle as water flows across the deck around it
A grey Navy helicopter with its rotors spinning hovers low above a ship's deck, and a deck crewman in a helmet and headset watches it from the bottom of the frame
Seen from high above, two helicopters with their main rotors turning sit on a ship's flight deck in open ocean, with a third helicopter at the far end of the deck
A wire rescue basket hangs on a hoist cable from a helicopter overhead, just above helmeted divers huddled in a yellow life raft at sea
A gray Navy helicopter hovers just above a ship's flight deck against a blue sky, its rotors spinning as it comes down to land or lifts off
A crew capsule topped with yellow balloons floats on churning water inside a flooded ship well deck, pushing waves against an orange frame while people watch from the walkways above
A gray military helicopter hovers low over open ocean with its main rotor spinning, nose toward the camera, under an overcast sky
Seen from above at the side of a ship, two black inflatable boats packed with crew bounce across choppy blue water and leave white wakes behind them.
A cable hangs down from a hovering helicopter to lift a person in a helmet off the water against a gray sky. Then a dark military helicopter flies low over the open sea.
A white rocket with a capsule on top starts to lift off its launch pad. Bright flames burst from its base beside the tall launch tower with its access arm, under a cloudy sky.
Seen from far away across water and a marsh, a rocket climbs above the launch pad on a long bright exhaust flame. Large white clouds of steam spread across the ground below it.
A white Dragon capsule with its nose cap hinged open moves through space with the docking port facing forward. The curve of the Earth, covered in clouds, is below it.
At dusk under a purple sky, a long orange multi-wheeled KAMAG transporter rolls down a paved road carrying a large white capsule with its headlights on.
At night, a white rocket rises past the tall launch tower beside it as bright flame and exhaust flood the base of the pad, before the footage cuts to black-and-white imagery.

Seen from far away across green marshland, a rocket lifts off its coastal pad in a billowing cloud of white smoke. The next shot is a close tracking view of the rocket climbing at a tilt through a hazy sky, with flames streaming from its engines.
A tall rocket with an orange core stage and two white side boosters fires its engines at liftoff beside the launch tower, as huge white exhaust clouds billow out across the pad.
A white NASA supersonic jet with a very long, needle-like nose rolls along a desert runway past hangars, and is then seen flying high above a dry lakebed.

A heavy-lift rocket fires its engines and clears the pad beside its tower in a burst of flame and smoke, then a wider shot follows it climbing high into the sky on a long flame trail above the exhaust clouds
Close shot of a large rocket climbing straight up on a long bright exhaust flame, with thick billowing clouds of exhaust smoke spreading across the launch pad and launch tower below it
Wide view from across water at hazy dawn of a rocket rising on a column of flame and smoke above the launch tower, while exhaust clouds roll across the pad below

Split-screen footage of a Mars landing. The top half looks up at a shiny foil-wrapped descent stage with its thrusters. The bottom half looks down at the rover hanging from cables as it is lowered toward the dusty ground below.
Real orbital footage: a white SpaceX Dragon capsule with its nose cone open hangs in black space, high above the bright, cloud-covered curve of Earth.
